One calm, dense, data-first look for every TKC screen.

Tokens are CSS custom properties (--tkc-*) that feed both the Angular shell theme and the legacy Dawn override. Everything on this page uses them. Change the brand hue above: the whole palette, all contrast ratios and every component follow from that one token (--tkc-brand-hue).

Angular = shell themeLegacy = Dawn override[custom] = needs Angular work

Colour Primitives hold the palette. Semantic tokens give it meaning. Components only use semantic tokens.

Proposal: one brand hueTKC has no brand palette yet. The brand colour is "harbour teal" (hue 195). It lives in one token, --tkc-brand-hue. The brand ramp, the neutrals (tinted with the brand hue), the navbar and focus ring all derive from it. Status colours (green, amber, red, blue, violet) keep fixed hues so meaning never changes with branding. Contrast was checked at hue 195; re-check after a hue swap (the ratios below recalculate live).

Brand colour options (SUITE-180, proposal) Three ways to bring the TKC Digital brand into the UI. Nothing here is applied: tokens.json is unchanged until the owner picks an option. Previews use local --bo-* variables scoped to this section.

Source of the brand coloursThe logo pink is #e95295 (oklch 0.66 0.195 356.5). The 2024 brand guide lists pink #EA4D94 and grey #737373 (with grey tints from 10% to 90%) and the typeface Roboto. The two pinks differ by less than 2 steps per channel. The logo file wins for the logo. The navbar and login previews use the real logo file (company_logo.svg, one colour, currentColor) in the logo pink.

Raw brand colours: why a darker step is needed

The brand pink and grey cannot be used as-is for text or button labels. This is true for every option.

A. Teal UI, pink only for the logo

Keep the draft teal as the UI primary. Add the brand pink as logo and accent tokens (--tkc-brand-pink, --tkc-logo). Pink is never used for text or for buttons.

Token impact. brand ramp stays hue 195. New: --tkc-brand-pink, --tkc-logo. Both modes: logo token = pink.

B. Pink is the primary hue

Change --tkc-brand-hue to 356.5. The brand ramp, tinted neutrals, navbar, links and focus ring all turn pink or plum. Primary buttons are pink.

C. Brand guide: grey UI, pink accent

Use the two brand-guide colours. Neutrals are pure grey (guide grey is #737373). Primary buttons are charcoal. Pink carries links, focus ring, selection tint and the logo. Pink is the accent, not the button colour.

Token impact. Neutral ramp loses its brand tint (chroma 0). primary-* maps to neutral steps. text-link-*, focus-ring, primary-subtle-* and the navbar indicator map to a new pink ramp. These tokens are already separate in tokens.json; only their mapping changes.

All pairs pass WCAG 2.2 AA.

Recommendation: option C (brand guide: grey UI, pink accent)

  • It is the brand. The guide has two colours, pink and grey. C is the only option that uses both as the guide does. A keeps a teal that is not in the brand. B uses pink for everything.
  • No clash with status colours. Pink (hue 356) sits next to danger red (hue 27). In B a pink Save button and a red Delete button look alike to many users. In C buttons are charcoal and pink marks links, focus and selection.
  • Contrast margin. All 72 pairs pass in all three options. B has the thinnest margin: its white label on the pink button is only 4.75:1 (needs 4.5:1). C has 11.73:1 on the button and 6.62:1 for pink links.
  • Logo. In every option the logo uses a new --tkc-logo token (the logo pink), not primary-default. Pink on white is 3.44:1. That passes the 3:1 graphic rule but not the text rule. Never set pink text on white.
  • Cost. C changes token mapping only: neutrals lose the teal tint, primary-* maps to neutral steps, links, focus ring and subtle colours map to a new pink ramp. No component change is needed. If the owner wants a more brand-forward look, B is the fallback.
  • Open point. The brand guide names Roboto. The draft system uses IBM Plex Sans. This is a separate decision and is not part of SUITE-180.

Typography IBM Plex Sans (SIL OFL, self-hostable) with a system fallback. IBM Plex Mono for IDs and reference numbers. Tabular numbers everywhere in data.
